items.title: Derek Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995
items.q: Derek went on to tour and record with Benny Goodman, Buddy DeFranco, and Benny Carter

ctx.x: Pianist Derek Smith was born in Stratford, England in 1931. A veteran of the RAF, he became a full time musician with the BBC and band leader Johnny Dankworth. He emigrated to the U.S. in 1957 and after a short period of non- music jobs he was able to record with Connie Kay and Percy Heath. Derek went on to tour and record with Benny Goodman, Buddy DeFranco, and Benny Carter, and held down the piano chair in the Tonight Show Band from 1967- 1974, moving with the group from New York to Los Angeles. We are here on behalf of the Hamilton College Jazz Archive Project on the Royal Caribbean cruise, and we’re talking with Derek Smith, a well traveled piano player who is performing this evening. And we’re here to get his thoughts on the state of jazz and his experiences in the jazz world. So welcome.
